tldr: An Oct 18 paper proposed hybrid agents that reason in latent space but act through text. A paper on Oct 27 then applied latent reasoning to multi-agent systems by storing reusable skills in compact external memory.
whats_new: No new latent-reasoning research landed after Oct 30; the Nov 4 item is a Latent Space newsletter that matched on name only, so the thread is still three unreplicated preprints.
why_it_matters: Latent reasoning aims to cut inference cost by keeping intermediate steps out of text, but it also makes those steps harder to inspect and log.

beats.headline: Hybrid agents think in latent space, act through text
beats.summary: Separates internal reasoning from the textual action interface.

beats.headline: SkillMem stores skills externally for latent multi-agent systems
beats.summary: Targets the mismatch between continuous reasoning and text-supplied skills.

beats.headline: Latent reasoning extends to unified multimodal models
beats.summary: Applies continuous-space reasoning to image understanding and generation.

beats.headline: Latent Space newsletter matched on name only
beats.summary: A quiet-day AINews issue; no latent-reasoning content.

open_questions: Do any of these papers report cost or latency savings against text chain-of-thought on the same tasks?
Is code or a model release available for the Hybrid Agents or SkillMem approaches?
take_for_builders: These are unreplicated preprints; if you log reasoning traces for debugging, check what your tooling would lose before adopting latent-reasoning models.
